title_ar: هل قراءة آيات من القرآن استهلالا لمحاضرة أو تذكيرا يجوز للحائض ؟
title_en: Is It Permissible for a Menstruating Woman to Recite Verses of the Qur'an to Open a Lecture or as an Exhortation?
body_ar: يجوز للحائض قراءة القرآن من حفظها في افتتاح الدروس و غيره لأن رفع مانعها ليس بيدها بخلاف الجنب.
body_en: It is permissible for a menstruating woman to recite the Qur'an from memory, at the opening of lessons and elsewhere, because the lifting of what bars her is not in her own hands — unlike the person in a state of major ritual impurity (junub).

flags.context: يجوز للحائض قراءة القرآن من حفظها
flags.note: This qualification is doing real work and must not be dropped. The permission as given covers reciting from memory. The Sheikh says nothing here about reading from a written copy or a screen, on which the Maliki position turns on touching the muṣḥaf; record 944 in this slice puts exactly that question about a phone and has no written answer. Nothing has been supplied for the case he did not address.

translator_notes: The reason given is the whole argument: a menstruating woman cannot end her state at will, whereas the junub can wash and so is not excused. The English keeps that contrast, which is the classical Maliki ground for the distinction.
The answer is short but complete — a question and a reasoned ruling — and is not a title-only stub.
